passages.title: The lovers speak and exchange praise
passages.summary: The woman asks to meet her lover. She describes vineyard work that her brothers forced upon her. She calls herself lovely despite the sun darkening her skin. She answers those who stare instead of accepting their judgment.
passages.uncertainty: The map locates named comparisons and groups. It does not trace the lovers’ movements.

lds.text: The Church’s Bible Dictionary reports the JST: “the Songs of Solomon are not inspired writings.” How does the woman answer those who stare at her skin?

passages.title: Spring brings an invitation
passages.summary: The lover calls the woman outside as spring arrives. She warns against awakening love before it desires. Flowers and ripening fruit express the pleasure of their meeting. Her warning places a limit beside that desire.
passages.uncertainty: The map locates named comparisons and groups. It does not trace the lovers’ movements.

lds.text: Why does the woman place a warning about love beside spring’s invitation?

passages.title: A night search and a royal carriage
passages.summary: The woman searches the streets and finds her lover. Another scene shows Solomon’s guarded wedding carriage. His mother gives him a wedding crown. Holding her lover answers the fear of losing him. The royal scene adds public wealth and protection.
passages.uncertainty: The map locates named comparisons and groups. It does not trace the lovers’ movements.

lds.text: How does the woman’s night search differ from Solomon’s guarded procession?

passages.title: Praise through animals, towers, and gardens
passages.summary: The lover praises the woman through many comparisons. She invites him into the garden. The garden describes the woman and their desire. These comparisons express praise rather than describe her literally.
passages.uncertainty: The map locates named comparisons and groups. It does not trace the lovers’ movements.

lds.text: What does the woman’s garden invitation add to the lover’s praise?

passages.title: A missed visit and a harmful search
passages.summary: The woman opens too late for her lover. Watchmen beat her and take her cloak during her search. Her search brings harm rather than help from city guards. She still asks the women to find her friend.
passages.uncertainty: The map locates named comparisons and groups. It does not trace the lovers’ movements.

passages.title: The women offer help
passages.summary: The women offer to seek the lover. He praises the woman above queens and other women. The women’s help answers her earlier request. His praise presents her as someone who cannot be replaced.
passages.uncertainty: The map locates named comparisons and groups. It does not trace the lovers’ movements.

lds.text: How does the women’s offer answer the request she made in chapter 5?

passages.title: The woman invites her lover outside
passages.summary: The lover praises the woman’s body through comparisons. She invites him to fields, villages, and vineyards. The woman states her desire and chooses a meeting place. Her voice directs their time together.
passages.uncertainty: The map locates named comparisons and groups. It does not trace the lovers’ movements.

lds.text: How does the woman take action after hearing the lover’s praise?

passages.title: Love, family control, and a woman’s answer
passages.summary: The poem compares love with death and fire. Brothers discuss their sister, and a woman answers for herself. Solomon rents out a vineyard. Wealth cannot buy the love described here. Her answer presents her own strength beside her brothers’ plans.

guides.title: Study Song of Solomon
guides.description: Follow selected chapters through the book.

steps.title: The lovers speak and exchange praise
steps.text: The woman asks to meet her lover. She describes vineyard work that her brothers forced upon her. She calls herself lovely despite the sun darkening her skin. She answers those who stare instead of accepting their judgment.

steps.title: A missed visit and a harmful search
steps.text: The woman opens too late for her lover. Watchmen beat her and take her cloak during her search. Her search brings harm rather than help from city guards. She still asks the women to find her friend.

steps.title: Love, family control, and a woman’s answer
steps.text: The poem compares love with death and fire. Brothers discuss their sister, and a woman answers for herself. Solomon rents out a vineyard. Wealth cannot buy the love described here. Her answer presents her own strength beside her brothers’ plans.
